extraction.name: DocVQA
extraction.description: A large scale dataset of 12,767 document images of varied types and content, over which 50,000 questions and answers are defined for Document Visual Question Answering.
extraction.creator: Minesh Mathew, Dimosthenis Karatzas, C.V. Jawahar
extraction.publisher: CVIT, IIIT Hyderabad, India; Computer Vision Center, UAB, Spain
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Images were sourced from the UCSF Industry Documents Library, and questions and answers were collected using remote workers via a web-based annotation tool.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Document analysis, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Documents from the UCSF Industry Documents Library, spanning 5 major industries (tobacco, food, drug, fossil fuel, and chemical).
extraction.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: Binarized images were minimized due to poor image quality, and pages with tables, forms, lists, and figures were prioritized over pages with only running text.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: The data was randomly split into train, validation, and test sets. For BERT models, OCR tokens were serialized to a single string separated by space in top-left to bottom-right order.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A three-stage process: Stage 1 involved workers defining up to 10 question-answer pairs per image. Stage 2 involved different workers verifying by answering the questions and assigning question types. Stage 3 involved authors reviewing and editing/accepting questions where Stage 1 and Stage 2 answers did not match.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Disagreements between the first and second stage annotators were resolved in a third stage review by the authors, who edited, accepted, or ignored the question-answer pairs.
extraction.rai:annotationsPerItem: At most 10 question-answer pairs per document image.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset collection process introduced sampling biases by deliberately minimizing binarized images and prioritizing pages with tables, forms, lists, and figures over pages that only have running text. Consequently, the dataset is also skewed towards documents from food and nutrition-related collections, as they contained a higher number of non-binarized images.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: Image quality issues due to binarization in the source library, and potential minor answer mismatches stemming from OCR errors.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Validation, and Testing for Document Visual Question Answering (DocVQA).

name.evidence: We present a new dataset for Visual Question Answering (VQA) on document images called DocVQA.

description.evidence: We introduce DocVQA, a large scale dataset of 12,767 document images of varied types and content, over which we have defined 50,000 questions and answers.

url.evidence: The dataset, code and leaderboard are available at docvqa.org

publisher.evidence: 1CVIT, IIIT Hyderabad, India2Computer Vision Center, UAB, Spain

rai:dataCollection.evidence: Images in the dataset are sourced from documents in UCSF Industry Documents Library... Questions and answers on the selected document images are collected with the help of remote workers, using a Web based annotation tool.

rai:dataCollectionType.evidence: Images in the dataset are sourced from documents in UCSF Industry Documents Library... Questions and answers on the selected document images are collected with the help of remote workers, using a Web based annotation tool.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: Images in the dataset are sourced from documents in UCSF Industry Documents Library. The documents are organized under different industries and further under different collections.

rai:dataManipulationProtocol.evidence: We tried to minimize binarized images in DocVQA since we did not want poor image quality to be a bottleneck for VQA. We also prioritized pages with tables, forms, lists and figures over pages which only have running text.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: The data is split randomly in an 80 10 10 ratio to train, validation and test splits... we first serialize the OCR tokens recognized on the document images to a single string, separated by space, in top-left to bottom-right order.

rai:dataAnnotationProtocol.evidence: The annotation process was organized in three stages. In stage 1, workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs on it... The second annotation stage aims to verify the data collected in the first stage... If none of the answers entered in the first stage match exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the particular question is sent for review in a third stage.

rai:dataAnnotationPlatform.evidence: Questions and answers on the selected document images are collected with the help of remote workers, using a Web based annotation tool.

rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis.evidence: If none of the answers entered in the first stage match exactly with any of the answers from the second stage, the particular question is sent for review in a third stage. Here questions and answers are editable and the reviewer either accepts the question-answer (after editing if necessary) or ignores it.

rai:annotationsPerItem.evidence: In stage 1, workers were shown a document image and asked to define at most 10 question-answer pairs on it.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: OCR tokens we use are extracted using a commercial OCR application.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: Majority of documents in the library are binarized and the binarization has taken on a toll on the image quality... Since no OCR is perfect, we propose to use ANLS as our primary evaluation metric, so that minor answer mismatches stemming from OCR errors are not severely penalized.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: The data is split randomly in an 80 10 10 ratio to train, validation and test splits.
